gaps.explanation: Statement pp5-6 Total Governmental Funds Total revenues 18,171,022 = General 8,721,279 + Economic Development 1,526,003 + Special Projects 1,060,589 + Debt Service 264,320 (p5) + Streets 3,946,385 + Capital Projects 1,219,066 + Other Governmental Funds 1,433,380 (p6). detail[] 12,604,948 = budget schedules General p13 8,531,766 + Economic Development p14 1,755,965 + Special Projects p15 883,837 + nonmajor combining pp16-17 1,433,380 (= Other Governmental Funds column). (1) Missing fund columns (no schedule, nothing in detail[]): Debt Service Fund (p5) Property taxes 1,222 + Special assessments 124,498 + Interest 138,600 = 264,320; Streets Fund (p6) Property taxes 531,034 + Sales taxes 524,669 + Miscellaneous taxes 2,326,622 + Intergovernmental 373,961 + Charges for services 2,211 + Interest 184,637 + Miscellaneous 3,251 = 3,946,385; Capital Projects Fund (p6) Property taxes 971,390 + Miscellaneous taxes 154,358 + Interest 93,318 = 1,219,066; total 5,429,771 (added). (2) Different basis (no fix): General budget p13 8,531,766 vs GAAP p5 8,721,279 = -189,513; Economic Development p14 1,755,965 vs p5 1,526,003 = +229,962; Special Projects p15 883,837 vs p5 1,060,589 = -176,752; net -136,303. Check: 12,604,948 + 5,429,771 + 136,303 = 18,171,022. After the fix the schedule stays 136,303 short, the budget-basis vs GAAP difference of these three funds. The Streets Fund's printed Proceeds from sale of capital asset 6 (p6) is added with the column as an other financing line (not revenue, not a transfer).
